full_judgment: 7. It is evident to this Court that bearing in mind the specific provisions of section 7 of the Act read with the rather exceptional provisions of section 7Ka this Court has been asked at the outset to determine the very existence of the arbitration agreement pursuant to which the notice dated 27-3-2007 was served upon the respondent (Annexure-'E'). In this regard, it is submitted that the measures as may be granted and adopted shall be in aid of the consequential arbitral proceedings in a manner that the decision of the Arbitral Tribunal and the award that it may make does not at the end of the day appear to be hollow. In other words, the purpose of any section 7Ka application is for the protection and preservation of the subject-matter of arbitral proceedings with a view to ensuring that any future award may remain effectively executable. For this Court to exercise its discretion under section 7Ka of the Act it is, in the view of this Court, sine qua non that there be a prima facie satisfaction that there has indeed, at one point in time or other been a meeting of minds between the parties to this Application to refer their disputes within a certain contractual selling to arbitration. The learned Advocate for the respondent Mr Md Ohiullah has vigorously argued by a reference to various precedents: 1996 2(SC) pages 667; AIR 1987 (SC) 1918; AIR 2000 (SC) 1379 and 1993 1 (SC) 230), that it would indeed, by various precedents be within the power and authority of this Court to determine the existence of an arbitration agreement. That notwithstanding, this Court is also mindful of the fact of the need to strike an essential balance between granting interim measures and the prudence in not encroaching upon any Arbitral Tribunal's ultimate authority to decide upon the existence, nature and scope of such arbitration agreement. Proceeding upon that cautionary note and examining in particular the document dated 12-9-2006 identified as "the contract" by the petitioner (Annexure-'A'), the Proforma Invoice of the following date relied upon and identified by the respondent to be the sole documentary evidence in support of any contractual arrangement between the parties, and the Letter of Credit and the amendments thereto as followed subsequently, it is this Court's view that these documents taken together establish a prima facie pattern of performance negotiation and course of conduct by the parties in this Application. The sequence with which the Proforma Invoice dated 13-9-2006 follows the document dated 12-9-2006 and identified by the petitioners as "the contract" within a span of 24 hours, the fact of such Proforma Invoice bearing the same reference number as that found on "the contract" itself i.e., 06/S/47071 and the fact of the unit price of US$ 387 per MT of the goods identified in the Proforma Invoice which can only properly be understood by reference to the explanation provided in the earlier document dated 12-9-2006 as being the price fixed net of the deposit already paid in advance by the petitioner for the goods otherwise regularly priced at US$ 407 per MT, have satisfied this Court that the contractual arrangement between the parties is one of a composite nature with "the contract" dated 12-9-2006 and the Proforma Invoice dated 13-9-2006 being the essential components thereof. The reference number found to be common to both these documents also, in the view of this Court, gives rise to a presumption of a contractual arrangement arrived at by means of necessary incorporation by reference whereby the arbitration clause found in the document dated 12-9-2006 may be read as being incorporated in the Proforma Invoice itself.
